_read_me: Copy this file to settings.json and fill it in. settings.json is ignored by git so your token never leaves your PC.
_follow_admins: Empty means follow every admin the scribe relays. Put names in to follow only some, e.g. ["Unraveller", "Brett"].
_allowed_symbols: NOT a filter any more - nothing is ever blocked by ticker, on his word ('no filters wanted'). This survives only as VOCABULARY: it helps the parser recognise a ticker typed in lowercase, like '40% in spy now'. Add words, never to block, only to read better.
_gone: trim_action, close_at_trim_pct, max_qty, max_trades_per_day, average_in, max_adds_per_position and dry_run_buying_power used to live here. Deleted, not defaulted - 'no filters wanted. id like to follow everything to the tee as they do.' Trims sell, adds follow, every call counts, and the test wallet is unlimited: it reports the most money tied up at once instead of refusing anything.

guards._hours: The window for NEW trades only. Exits are always allowed whatever the clock says - you never want to be stuck in something because it's one minute past.

_execution: dryrun = log it, send nothing. webull = real options orders in your Webull account. Use START HERE number 2 rather than editing this by hand.

execution._futures_enabled: THE futures switch. false = his NQ/ES calls are read, priced and logged, and nothing ever fires. true = they trade: pretend money in dry run, ONE real contract at a time in live. Leave false until the Webull futures data subscription is live. The popup's Settings flips this for you.
execution._assume_weekly_expiry: Their pinned rules say contracts are weekly unless they spell out 0DTE or a date, so a call like 'in SPY 747C @ 3.00' with no date on it means this Friday. true = fill that in. false = refuse those calls instead. Only ever used on an entry that already named a strike - an exit always uses the contract you are actually holding, never a guess.
execution._reset_paper_daily: Clear all paper/dry-run positions at New York midnight so the popup starts each day with a clean paper book. Live (real-money) positions are never touched. true = clear daily, false = carry paper positions over.
execution._ai_reader: READING intelligence for the calls the regex can't crack. Only runs on a MISSED message: hands that one line to Claude, which reads it into a clean call that still passes every guard (a made-up ticker is refused). It never decides to trade. enabled+api_key set it; the popup does this for you. Empty key = off, no cost.

webull._account_id: Blank means pick the options account automatically. It will never use a futures account.
webull._futures_account_id: Your Webull FUTURES account number, so MNQ/MES orders route there instead of your options account (Webull rejects futures on a non-futures account). Blank = auto-detect by type/suffix, which fails when Webull labels the futures account as MARGIN.
webull._entry_price: Where your buy order sits. Webull takes no market orders on options, so this is always a limit. bid = sit on the bid and wait for a seller to come down to you - cheapest, and on a call that runs straight from the message you will not get filled at all. mid = halfway between bid and ask. ask = pay the offer plus marketable_buffer_pct, which is what fills nearly every time.
webull._entry_fill_seconds: How long your bid is allowed to sit there before it gets pulled. An entry left resting all day can fill at 3:55pm into a trade they called at 9:40 and were out of by 10:05 - you would be buying their exit. 180 = 3 minutes, enough for a cheap contract to actually get hit.
webull._stop_loss_pct: The stop, as a % off what YOU actually paid - not off the price they posted. 20 means a fill at 2.80 gets a stop at 2.24. It is held two ways: a real stop order resting at Webull, and a watchdog in bridge.py checking the bid. Whichever sees it first sells, and only one of them is allowed to. On options premium 20% is tight - it is a normal amount of movement on a slow morning.
webull._fill_poll_seconds: How often the bridge asks whether your bid filled, and how often the stop watchdog checks the bid. 5 is fine. Lower is faster and asks Webull for more quotes.
webull._keep_cash_buffer: Dollars to never touch, in a live account. 0 spends everything available. 50 means an entry is skipped once it would leave you under $50.
webull._paper_trading: Paper is the TEST ENGINE: every non-live room fills in your Webull SIMULATED (sandbox) account for real prices, still scored per room. It turns on automatically the moment a sandbox key is saved (leave paper_trading unset for that auto behaviour, or set it false by hand to force the in-house sim instead). Webull's sandbox is FULLY ISOLATED from your live account and needs its OWN app key/secret (a separate developer application, auto-approved in minutes) — your live keys will NOT work there. Paste the sandbox keys as paper_app_key/paper_app_secret (popup PAPER boxes or setup_keys). paper_endpoint defaults to api.sandbox.webull.com; paper_account_id names a specific sim account if you have more than one.

_simulation: Honest test-mode fills and optional tactics, all OFF by default. realistic_fills subtracts real per-contract fees. entry_offset_dollars bids that much under their price (0.05 = $5/option). auto_breakeven sells sell_fraction at +at_pct and moves the stop to breakeven. auto_ladder runs YOUR own exit on their entry: trims at each rung's at%, keeps keep_runners contracts, and drags the stop to fill*(1+stop_to/100) (stop_to null = leave it). Default plan: +10% same stop, +20% breakeven, +30% lock +10%, keep 2. Flip these in the popup's Realism & tactics section.
